111.75000,40.82000.desc: A medical institution approved by China's National Health Commission to perform assisted reproduction. Approved for: ICSI — a single sperm injected into the egg; IVF with embryo transfer; embryo screening before transfer; insemination with donor sperm; insemination with the partner's sperm. All of its approvals are in formal operation. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Approval is compulsory in China and performing assisted reproduction without it is unlawful, so this list is a register rather than a directory of members. It names every approved institution in the country, which is more than almost any other state publishes. The address did not geocode, so this point sits at the centre of the province rather than at the institution.

103.78138,1.29628.name: Defence Medical and Environmental Research Institute
103.78138,1.29628.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by DSO National Laboratories. It is categorised as a defense laboratory, working on both human and animal health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-93.26500,44.97780.name: National Marrow Donor Program / NMDP (United States) — cell therapy infrastructure
-93.26500,44.97780.desc: The US registry through which unrelated stem cell donors are matched to patients, and the infrastructure gene therapies for blood disorders depend on. Casgevy and its equivalents need the same capability — conditioning, apheresis, a specialist transplant unit — so a cure delivered as edited cells can only reach patients where that system already exists, which is a smaller map than the disease.

-93.26500,44.97780.name: Cargill and Archer Daniels Midland — the exporters' separate claims
-93.26500,44.97780.state: Minnetonka and Chicago — the grain exporters
-93.26500,44.97780.desc: The two largest grain traders were suing the same company over the same events and were expressly excluded from the farmers' settlement, pursuing their claims separately. That separation is the entry. When an unapproved trait reaches an export market, the loss lands on at least three groups with different interests — farmers who never planted it, handlers and ethanol plants who moved it, and the exporters whose cargoes were turned away — and they do not litigate together. A reader tracing who bears the cost of a premature release should expect to find several separate actions rather than one, and the farmers' class is usually the slowest and the largest.

-93.26500,44.97780.name: Vaxxinova
-93.26500,44.97780.desc: A veterinary vaccine company built around autogenous vaccines — vaccines made from pathogens isolated on one particular farm, for that farm, on a veterinarian's prescription, rather than licensed for general sale. It also sells a patented technology that raises antibodies against the iron-transport proteins of bacteria, starving them of an essential nutrient. Autogenous production belongs on this map because of what it does to the record: a product made for a single herd from a locally isolated organism does not go through the approval process a licensed vaccine does, so it appears in no national register of authorised products. The organism is engineered or selected, administered to livestock, and effectively invisible to the registers this map is otherwise built from.

-73.93300,40.70400.name: Genspace
-73.93300,40.70400.desc: The first community biology laboratory, in Brooklyn, offering benchwork to people with no institution behind them. Community labs are where the safety argument is most visible, because they have no institutional biosafety committee to answer to and have generally built their own instead.

-86.58600,34.73000.name: Aviagen
-86.58600,34.73000.desc: Supplies the broiler genetics behind a very large share of the chicken eaten worldwide, under EW Group ownership. Almost every commercial chicken descends from a handful of proprietary breeding lines held by two companies, which is the narrowest genetic bottleneck in any food animal and predates engineering entirely.
